## Overview

Preserve FunctionGemma `<escape>`-delimited argument values as strings instead of decoding them as JSON scalars or containers, unless the tool's parameter schema declares a non-string type for that argument. Fixes #63906 for streaming and non-streaming chat completions.

## Claims

- Escaped numeric, boolean, null, JSON-container and quoted text keeps its literal string value when the parameter is declared `string` or has no schema.
- Arguments whose schema declares a non-string type (`integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, `null`) are still converted, so typed arguments keep working, including when the bundled chat template wraps them in `<escape>` (see Details).
- The change is confined to the FunctionGemma argument parser and reuses the shared `find_tool_properties` / `extract_types_from_schema` / `coerce_to_schema_type` helpers; no shared parser interfaces or generation logic change.

## Validation

Python sources: main `8701c9b75`. Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, Torch 2.14.0+cu132, 1x H200 NVL. No native code changed.

`tests/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py` (CPU only), the same test file on three versions of the parser:

| Parser | strings stay strings (#63906) | declared non-string types convert |
|---|---|---|
| main | 16 failed | pass (except `42` with no schema, which became `42`) |
| first revision of this PR (strings only) | pass | 5 failed (`integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `null` returned as strings) |
| this PR | pass | pass |

Whole file with this PR: `40 passed`.

`tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py` (OpenAI HTTP server, six string values × streaming/non-streaming): `12 failed` on main (e.g. `assert {'value': 123} == {'value': '123'}`), `12 passed` with this PR.

```sh
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 pytest tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_functiongemma_tool_parser.py -q
```

The HTTP regression uses real `Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct` weights and an exact structured-output regex to produce the FunctionGemma wire format. It exercises actual GPU decoding, the OpenAI server, and FunctionGemma parsing deterministically. This is a serving-format evaluation, not an evaluation of FunctionGemma's natural tool-selection accuracy. Access to Google's gated checkpoint returned 401, so no FunctionGemma-model accuracy claim is made.

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Existing CPU tool-parser and API Server Generate Buildkite steps select the tests and depend on the changed source path.

## Details

Google's [format specification](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/functiongemma/formatting-and-best-practices#delimiter_for_string_values_escape) defines `<escape>` as a string delimiter. `_parse_arguments` was applying `json.loads` to the text inside those delimiters, changing values such as `123`, `true`, `null`, `[1,2]`, `{"x":1}` and `"quoted"` even for parameters declared as `string`.

Keeping every escaped value as a string would regress typed parameters, though: `examples/tool_chat_template_functiongemma.jinja` renders every earlier tool-call argument as `key:<escape>value<escape>`, including integers and booleans, so a model following that history can emit `count:<escape>42<escape>` for an `integer` parameter, which the old `json.loads` turned back into `42`. The parser therefore follows the declared schema type, the same way the K2 Horizon parser does: `string` or no schema keeps the literal text, other declared types are converted, and a value that doesn't convert stays a string. Making the template escape only string values would match Google's format more closely, but it would also need the parser to accept unescaped values, which is out of scope here.

This does not add support for unescaped non-string arguments.

Duplicate-work audit inspected actual diffs and discussions for #48705 (multi-key streaming concatenation), #59754 (single-delta calls), #57768 (regex timeout), #57989 (hyphenated names), #57120 (surrounding content), and #47254 (Rust parser). None implements this escaped-string semantic correction. Related general parser PRs #63385 and #54964 also do not change this path.

AI assistance was used for the investigation, implementation, tests and this description.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+
+MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def server():
+    # Constrain a small public model to the FunctionGemma wire format. This
+    # isolates serving/parser behavior from model tool-selection accuracy.
+    args = [
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--enable-auto-tool-choice",
+        "--tool-call-parser",
+        "functiongemma",
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "1024",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "2",
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.1",
+    ]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(MODEL, args, max_wait_seconds=480) as server:
+        yield server
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stream", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "value", ["123", "true", "null", "[1,2]", '{"x":1}', '"quoted"']
+)
+def test_escape_delimited_strings_over_http(server, stream, value):
+    output = (
+        "<start_function_call>call:lookup{value:<escape>"
+        f"{value}<escape>}}<end_function_call>"
+    )
+    tools = [
+        {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {
+                "name": "lookup",
+                "parameters": {
+                    "type": "object",
+                    "properties": {"value": {"type": "string"}},
+                    "required": ["value"],
+                },
+            },
+        }
+    ]
+    with server.get_client() as client:
+        response = client.chat.completions.create(
+            model=MODEL,
+            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Call lookup."}],
+            tools=tools,
+            tool_choice="auto",
+            temperature=0,
+            max_tokens=128,
+            stream=stream,
+            extra_body={"structured_outputs": {"regex": re.escape(output)}},
+        )
+        if stream:
+            arguments = ""
+            names = []
+            for chunk in response:
+                for call in chunk.choices[0].delta.tool_calls or []:
+                    assert call.index == 0
+                    if call.function.name:
+                        names.append(call.function.name)
+                    arguments += call.function.arguments or ""
+            assert names == ["lookup"]
+        else:
+            calls = response.choices[0].message.tool_calls
+            assert calls is not None and len(calls) == 1
+            assert calls[0].function.name == "lookup"
+            arguments = calls[0].function.arguments
+    assert json.loads(arguments) == {"value": value}
